summary: Iteration 54 — Verified Social.docx Issue #6 `NeedsKyc` guard on /driver/kyc/*. Backend request-otp / verify-otp return correct next_step for all 3 driver states. Full UI verification: APPROVED driver (drv_seed_appr1 / +919999900003) is redirected from ALL 8 KYC routes (personal, id, licence, selfie, vehicle, bank, emergency, submitted) to /driver/dashboard, and the dashboard renders with data-testid=driver-dashboard. PENDING driver (+919999900002) and ONBOARDING driver (+919999900001) can still render every KYC route — NeedsKyc correctly does NOT bounce them. Unauthenticated user visiting /driver/kyc/personal is redirected to /driver/login (falls back to auth check).
critical_code_review_comments: NeedsKyc implementation is clean & correctly composes with the existing auth check (loading -> unauth -> approved-bounce -> render).
DriverApp.jsx is 1441 lines — split into smaller modules (auth/context, KYC steps, dashboard, guards) for maintainability.

context_for_next_testing_agent: NeedsKyc guard at DriverApp.jsx:1398 is verified. Login token stored in localStorage['baked_driver_token']. Backend /api/driver/auth/{request-otp,verify-otp} use `phone_e164` field. verify-otp payload is {phone_e164, code} — NOT otp_id. next_step logic: approved->dashboard, pending_review->submitted, onboarding->vehicle. For UI-only guard tests you can inject the token directly via localStorage and navigate — no need to complete full OTP UI flow.
rca of the issue: Fixed already by main agent — old NeedsAuth wrapper allowed approved drivers to view KYC pages via stale links/bookmarks. New NeedsKyc guard adds a `driver.status === 'approved'` early-exit that <Navigate to='/driver/dashboard' replace />, closing the loop-back.
